neet_phy_u14_t07_1.working: In a pure inductor the current lags the voltage by 90°, so cos φ = 0 and P = V_rms·I_rms·cos 90° = 0.

neet_phy_u14_t07_3.working: cos φ = 0.6 gives sin φ = 0.8. Wattless current = I_rms·sin φ = 10 × 0.8 = 8 A.

neet_phy_u14_t07_4.working: A: pure inductor has φ = 90°, so pf = 0 (III). B: at resonance the circuit is purely resistive, so pf = 1 (I). C: Z = √(30² + 40²) = 50 Ω, so pf = 30/50 = 0.6 (II). D: with R = X_L, φ = 45°, so pf ≈ 0.707 (IV).

neet_phy_u14_t07_5.working: A is true: cos φ = R/Z. B is true: only the resistor dissipates power, so P = I_rms²R. C is false: a low pf needs a larger current for the same power. D is true: capacitors offset inductive loads and raise the pf. E is false: the wattless component is 90° out of phase with the voltage. Correct set: A, B, D.
